subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw add Control UI save-time MEMORY.md budget enforcement and archive assistance, or keep current `/context`, doctor, and prompt diagnostics as the supported boundary?
rationale: Current source already covers post-truncation and diagnostic visibility, but refusing saves and moving content into an archive introduce new user workflow and memory-ownership semantics that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Add bounded Control UI enforcement
options.body: Implement a visible current/max budget meter plus warning or blocking behavior for bootstrap files, and keep archive automation as a separately scoped follow-up.

options.title: Keep diagnostics-only boundary
options.body: Treat `/context`, prompt warnings, doctor, and docs as the supported behavior and close or narrow enforcement/archive requests after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Fold into memory lifecycle design
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42877 or a successor design to specify bounded writes, consolidation, and archive semantics before changing the Control UI save path.

recommendation.title: Add bounded Control UI enforcement
recommendation.body: Implement a visible current/max budget meter plus warning or blocking behavior for bootstrap files, and keep archive automation as a separately scoped follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work touches both the bootstrap diagnostics and the file-save surfaces most likely to host the decision.
